mcat_description.short: Log cabins are prefabricated or custom-built wooden structures assembled from stacked or interlocked solid logs or engineered timber, sold as complete habitable units for residential, hospitality, and eco-tourism use.
mcat_description.long: A log cabin is a structure whose walls are formed from horizontally stacked solid wood logs or engineered timber, providing natural insulation, structural strength, and a distinctive rustic aesthetic. In the Indian market, log cabins are predominantly supplied as prefabricated or modular units — factory-manufactured in sections and assembled on-site — targeting resort developers, eco-tourism operators, hill-station homeowners, and farmhouse builders. Wood species used in Indian market supply include imported kiln-dried Canadian spruce, pine (SPF), and cedar, with treatment processes applied for moisture, termite, and weather resistance. Buyers typically commission custom-dimensioned structures quoted per square foot, with design, manufacturing, and installation offered as an end-to-end service.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, log cabins are primarily positioned as prefabricated or modular wooden structures for the hospitality, eco-tourism, and premium residential segments, with demand concentrated in hill stations, forest-adjacent resorts, and farmhouse developments. Leading Indian manufacturers (e.g. Deodar Group, Royal Prefab/Wooden Home India, Wooden Villas India, Prefab Wooden Homes) supply end-to-end services covering design, factory fabrication, and on-site installation. Wood sourcing in the Indian market relies heavily on imported kiln-dried timber — Canadian spruce, SPF (spruce-pine-fir), and pine — with PEFC/FSC-certified supply chains cited by multiple manufacturers; cedar is preferred for humid and coastal climates due to its natural moisture and insect resistance. Properly treated log homes are cited by multiple Indian manufacturers as lasting 50–80 years or more. The market distinguishes between modular prefab cabins (factory-built panels assembled on-site), portable/relocatable cabins (skid-mounted, standard sizes), and fully handcrafted on-site log homes. Buyer vocabulary in India uses 'log cabin', 'wooden cabin', 'log home', and 'resort cottage' interchangeably; 'chalet' and 'eco cabin' are used in hospitality contexts. The 'nap pod' and 'Sonabath cabin' signals observed in keyword and call data are contamination from misplaced listings and do not represent the primary buyer segment.
